entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: Socialist realism in Poland was a socio-political and aesthetic doctrine sanctioned by the pro-Soviet government of the post-war Polish People’s Republic during its campaign of Stalinization. The policy prescribing its use for institutional aesthetics was introduced in 1949 by decree of the Polish United Workers' Party minister Włodzimierz Sokorski, who would later become, Minister of Culture and Art. As in all Eastern Bloc countries in the Soviet sphere of influence, Socialist realism was utilized by the State as an instrument in the social engineering of Polish society and labour culture.
